Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

great adjective and interjection

excellent, very good

also Great!, excellent, terrific, fantastic, that’s great

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 2.4.2: puer optimus
Ter. Ad. 983: Ō vir optime.

optimus, optima, optimum

adjective, superlative of bonus

excellent, very good, great

In praise of a person or a thing Latin uses the superlative of bonus: puer optimus, a great boy.

Other words

  • Optimē! — Great! Excellent!

    adverb, used as an exclamation · classical · Ter. Ad. 884: Optimē est.; Plaut. Most. 449c: Factum optimē.

    The answer to good news: optimē est, that’s great; factum optimē, of something that has turned out well.

  • euge — bravo! great!

    interjection · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 241b: Euge euge, lepidē; Traupman 18, 392

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; also Pers., Mart.)

    Applause for a plan or a deed (see well done).

  • probē — good! right! excellent!

    adverb, used as an exclamation · also used · classical · Ter. And. 416–418: Ehem, pater. — Probē.; Traupman 18: Probē! Euge!

  • ēgregius, ēgregia, ēgregium — outstanding, excellent

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 69: vir ēgregius (Lewis & Short)

    “Chosen from the herd” (ē grege, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Ō Syre noster, salvē: quid fit? quid agitur? — Rēctē. — Optimē est.

    Syrus, my friend, hello! What’s new? How are things? — Fine. — Great.Ter. Ad. 883–884

  • usquīn valuistī? — Usque ut vidēs. — Factum optimē.

    Have you been well all along? — As you see. — Great.Plaut. Most. 448–449c

  • Euge euge, lepidē, laudō commentum tuom.

    Great, great, very neat: I like your plan.Plaut. Mil. 241b

See also well done, nice, big.
